function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact spot price of gold for today.  The most reliable way to get the current U.S. gold price is to check a reputable financial news or market data site that updates continuously, such as:

| Source | Typical update frequency | How to access |
|--------|--------------------------|---------------|
| **Bloomberg** | Every few seconds | Bloomberg.com/markets or the Bloomberg terminal |
| **Kitco** | Every minute | kitco.com |
| **Reuters** | Every few seconds | Reuters.com/markets |
| **Investing.com** | Every minute | investing.com/commodities/gold |
| **U.S. Treasury / Federal Reserve** | Daily close | treasury.gov or fedsystems.gov |

If you need the price for a specific time (e.g., the closing price on a particular day), most of these sites provide historical charts where you can zoom in to the exact minute.  

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use a search engine query like “gold price today” or “gold spot price” and it will usually display the latest figure from one of the above sources.
